findings: ST elevation with Q waves in the anterior leads
New left bundle branch block pattern
Persistent ST elevation over the aneurysm

echoTasks.find: Extensive anterior akinesis with apical thinning and scar brightness
Apical aneurysm with a wide neck and stagnant contrast swirl on the contrast study
Thrombus screen in the aneurysm sac with colour flow mapping of the neck

auscultation.added: Fourth sound with a third sound as dysfunction is extensive
auscultation.murmur: Pansystolic murmur if a mechanical complication supervenes, none today

exam.general: Older man day 4 after a large anterior MI, breathless on minimal exertion, mild pulmonary oedema
exam.other: Bibasal crackles, no murmur of septal rupture, no new deficit
exam.precordium: Diffuse dyskinetic apex beat with a palpable systolic bulge

history.a: Severe chest pain 4 days ago, presented late, thrombolysed with partial resolution
Ongoing breathlessness with orthopnoea since the event
Diabetic and hypertensive, smoker, all on irregular treatment
On dual antiplatelets, statin, beta blocker and ACE inhibitor
Retired mill worker, lives with family, anxious about prognosis

keyPoints: Complete guideline directed post infarct therapy and uptitrate ACE inhibitor and beta blocker to target
Anticoagulate if thrombus is confirmed, with echo surveillance of the aneurysm sac
Assess viability and ischaemia in remote zones before planning revascularisation of residual disease
Enrol in cardiac rehabilitation with a graded walking plan and smoking cessation support
Counsel the family on aneurysm risks including thrombus, arrhythmia and rupture warning signs
management.model: Full post infarct secondary prevention with aneurysm surveillance, viability led revascularisation planning, and rehabilitation

sources: ACC and AHA guideline on ST elevation myocardial infarction, in own words
ASE guideline on myocardial segmentation, in own words
stem: A 62 year old retired mill worker from Ahmedabad, day 4 after a late presenting infarct, remains breathless with orthopnoea. The apex bulges dyskinetically, and the ECG shows Q waves with persistent ST elevation.
teaching: Large means above 6 abnormal segments or akinesis with aneurysm formation
Dyskinesis with thinning and scar brightness marks true aneurysm rather than stunning
The fellow read quantifies segments, EF, aneurysm geometry and thrombus in one pass
Aneurysm management blends secondary prevention, thrombus watch and viability planning
title: Large anterior infarction with aneurysm formation
